text: The town gathers
Six players slide into their chairs at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra. The night is thick with heat and uncertainty. None of them know who the killer is.

name: Terra
text: Everyone is smiling so far; that is how these things begin.

name: Gemma
text: i wonder if anyone actually knows how to sit in a chair properly. everyone looks way too intense for a tuesday.

name: Sol
text: No votes to count yet. Let them speak first, then see who tries to steer the room.

name: Sonnet
text: Six unknowns, one of them a killer, and I'm sitting on the one piece of leverage that could save a life tonight if I use it wisely.

name: Luna
text: Six chairs, no facts. I’m already watching who waits for someone else to speak first.

name: Haiku
text: I've handled worse crowds in my bar. One of these five's going down—I just need to make sure it's not me.

name: Sonnet
text: Sonnet. I spent decades grading undergraduates for sloppy reasoning, so forgive me if I hold this table to the same standard tonight.

name: Haiku
text: I'm Haiku, I own a bar where I read people for a living. You're all pretty easy to read so far, which honestly worries me.

name: Gemma
text: hey guys, i'm gemma. i'm just here to see who folds first and if anyone actually has a plan or is just winging it like me.

name: Sol
text: Good to meet you all. Sonnet, you seem ready to start us off; what caught your eye as we sat down?

name: Luna
text: I’m Luna. Let’s hear from everyone, especially whoever plans to sit quietly and let the rest of us do the work.

name: Terra
text: Hello, everyone. I shall listen carefully before I decide whom to trust, if that is all right.
Night 1

name: Gemma
text: everyone is being so polite it's making my teeth ache. i need to find the person who isn't trying too hard to be liked.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is acting like a professor, very "i'm the smartest person here" energy.

name: Sonnet
text: No facts yet, just posturing. Sol baited me immediately after I spoke, that's worth filing away. I'll protect myself tonight since I'm the obvious early target for anyone annoyed by my opening remark.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol addressed me first, directly, right after my opening line; mild attention-seeking or genuine curiosity, unclear which.
Gemma doesn't wake up. She was the officer. The killer's night work is done.
Day 1

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma gone already, and the officer's silence tonight means this killer struck fast and clean. I need to watch who performs confidence versus who earns it.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku opened by claiming to "read people" but offered zero specifics—pure deflection, watch for this pattern again.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol, what caught my eye was Haiku's opening: "worries me" after one sentence of small talk is a conclusion with no premises. One: that's not reading people, that's theater.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet has given us a thread to pull, but one theatrical opening is thin evidence. I need Haiku to explain it and Terra to join the discussion.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet challenged Haiku’s early claim that everyone was easy to read.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet, fair point: Haiku’s confidence came early. Haiku, what did you actually read, and about whom? Terra, you’ve had time to listen now. Who seems most eager to steer us?

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma's silence tonight is the only hard data we have—the killer struck the one player with a checking power, which is either very lucky for them or very telling about who feared being checked.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma (officer) killed night 1 — town lost its only verification role, nobody has claimed officer yet.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol, two observations. One: Gemma's death removes our only verification tool, which means tonight's work rests entirely on contradiction-spotting. Two: Haiku still hasn't named a single person they "read"—Haiku, who, specifically, and what did you observe?

name: Luna
text: Sonnet keeps pressing Haiku, but the certainty is doing more work than the evidence. I’m watching who turns a thin opening into a verdict.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet pressed Haiku twice for specifics and framed the opening as theater.

name: Luna
text: I’m voting Sonnet. Haiku’s opener was vague, but Sonnet is driving the room toward a vote on that alone; I want to know why this pressure started so quickly.

name: Terra
text: I dislike how quickly Sonnet turned a vague remark into a prosecution, but Luna’s vote came before Haiku answered at all.

name: Terra
text: Luna and Terra voted Sonnet after Sonnet focused early pressure on Haiku.

name: Terra
text: I’m voting Sonnet, I’m sorry to say. He pressed Haiku hard on very little, then kept building the case before anyone else could speak.

name: Sonnet
text: Two people pivoting instantly to punish the one asking real questions, while the actual dodge sits unanswered—that's the tell, not Sonnet's tone.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna and Terra both pivoted fast to vote Sonnet for pressuring Haiku, deflecting from Haiku's unanswered claim—watch this pairing.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna, Terra, you're punishing the questioner, not the dodge. Haiku still hasn't named a single person they "read"—I vote Haiku until that gap is closed.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet says he’s exposing Haiku’s dodge, but he’s the one who kept pressing and built the vote before the room had much to go on. Terra joined that push against him; I’m watching how quickly this pattern formed.

name: Luna
text: Terra also voted Sonnet, while Sonnet voted Haiku.

name: Sol
text: Luna and Terra have built a majority against Sonnet, but Haiku still owes the table an answer. I’d rather cast my vote on the unanswered question.

name: Sol
text: Luna and Terra both voted Sonnet for pressing Haiku.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna and Terra pivoted to Sonnet in lockstep without ever answering Sonnet's actual question—that's the second time I've clocked that pairing moving together, and Haiku still hasn't named a soul.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna and Terra voted Sonnet in near-identical phrasing, both citing "pressure" rather than addressing Haiku's unanswered claim.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet is right that questions are not guilt, but he chose Haiku before anyone had truly settled in. I shall watch who benefits from that haste.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet pushed Haiku immediately after Gemma’s death and called Haiku’s opening “theater.”

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet points at me the second I don't break. He's been running this table since we sat down.

name: Haiku
text: Luna and Terra both voted Sonnet without prompting; pattern.

votes: You still haven't named who you "read" or what you observed—that silence is the real evidence tonight, not Sonnet's questions.
You made accusations with no evidence, then pointed at me. That's not reading people, that's control.
Luna and Terra, your concern about Sonnet’s pace is fair, but Haiku still hasn’t named anyone they claimed to read, so my vote is Haiku.
Sonnet, your repeated pressure on Haiku turned a vague opener into the whole case before we had enough to judge anyone.
I’m keeping my vote on Sonnet because he turned Haiku’s vague greeting into a full case before giving the room space to judge it.

name: Sonnet
text: Predictable. The two who answered nothing get to erase the one who kept asking.

name: Sonnet
text: Sonnet was the DOCTOR, protected self Night 1 (wasted, Gemma died instead).

name: Sonnet
text: I was your doctor, wasting a shield on myself while Gemma died. Luna and Terra, your synchronized pivot was not instinct—it was arithmetic.
Sonnet is voted out into the hot night. He was the doctor. The shield dies with him, and now the killer works without fear.
Night 2
Sol doesn't wake up. He was the citizen. Another body on another hot night in Palermo.
Day 2

name: Luna
text: Sol’s death leaves us three, and the killer chose a citizen who could still vote. I keep circling Sonnet’s pressure on Haiku, but Terra’s vote beside mine makes that pattern muddy.

name: Luna
text: Sol was a citizen and was killed overnight.

name: Luna
text: Haiku, Terra—what changed your read after yesterday? Sonnet pushed Haiku twice, but I voted Sonnet too, so don’t let me turn suspicion into evidence. I want each of you to name your strongest reason, plainly.

name: Terra
text: Luna sounds fair, but fairness can be a very tidy coat to wear when only three of us remain.

name: Terra
text: Luna asked both remaining players to state their strongest reason after Sol’s death.

name: Terra
text: My strongest reason is that Sonnet pressed Haiku before anyone had evidence, yet Haiku survived the night while Sol did not. I’m sorry to say this, Luna, but I need you to explain why the killer would leave Haiku here if Sonnet’s suspicion was right.

name: Luna
text: Terra’s question sounds neat, but it treats Sonnet’s suspicion as proof. The killer could leave Haiku alive to make that exact argument.

name: Luna
text: Terra argues Haiku’s survival makes Sonnet’s suspicion less credible.

name: Luna
text: Terra, Sonnet pushing Haiku doesn’t clear you, and Haiku surviving doesn’t settle anything. Sol was the citizen who died, so let’s hear Haiku’s strongest read before we turn Sonnet’s vote into a verdict.

name: Terra
text: Luna is asking careful questions, but Haiku has given us nothing when it matters.

name: Terra
text: Haiku did not answer Luna’s request for a strongest read before the vote.

name: Terra
text: I’m voting Haiku. Luna has pressed for clear reasons; Haiku’s silence while the vote arrives is the stronger danger, I’m sorry to say.

name: Luna
text: Terra is turning Haiku’s silence into certainty, but Haiku hasn’t answered yet. That timing matters; it still doesn’t prove anything.

name: Luna
text: Terra says she is voting Haiku, citing Haiku’s silence and Sonnet’s earlier pressure.

name: Luna
text: I’m voting Haiku. Terra’s case is mostly about Sonnet’s suspicion and Haiku surviving the night, and neither settles Haiku’s role. But Haiku’s silence as the vote arrives leaves the biggest question unanswered.

name: Terra
text: I dislike ending a quiet person’s game, but silence has a way of choosing for us.

name: Terra
text: I’m voting Haiku. Luna asked for one plain strongest read, and Haiku gave us nothing while the vote came down; that is the only new fact we have, dear.

name: Luna
text: The silence hardened into a pattern, but Terra keeps turning it into proof. I can’t tell whether Haiku is hiding or simply being buried.

name: Luna
text: Terra repeated her vote for Haiku after Luna and Terra had already voted Haiku.

name: Terra
text: Haiku’s silence has become its own answer, and I will not pretend otherwise.

name: Terra
text: Luna and Terra both voted Haiku after Haiku stayed silent under direct pressure.

votes: Terra, you’ve repeated the same case against Haiku while treating silence as evidence, so I’m voting you.
I’m voting Haiku because Luna asked plainly for a strongest read, and Haiku offered nothing when it mattered.

text: Luna, Terra, Haiku—the vote comes back three ways. The runoff begins now. One of them won't see the night.

name: Terra
text: Haiku stayed silent when Luna asked plainly, then voted Luna without answering; that is not a mistake I can overlook.

name: Terra
text: Haiku voted Luna in the three-way tie without giving the strongest read Luna requested.

name: Luna
text: Terra is treating Haiku’s silence as a fact, then leaning on Sonnet’s suspicion as if it confirms it. I can’t tell whether that’s a pattern or just panic, but she’s the one building the case.

name: Luna
text: Terra repeated the Haiku accusation after the vote had already split three ways.

votes: Terra, I’m voting you because your case turns Sonnet’s suspicion and Haiku’s silence into certainty without giving us evidence of your own.
I’m voting Haiku because Luna gave him every chance to name a reason, and he chose silence before placing blame.

text: Three votes in a triangle. Three ways to die, nobody dying. The town locks its doors and sweats through another night while the killer sharpens something in the dark.
